document.description: A resident app that connects local bookings, service requests, community notices, and polls through a shared mobile interface.
document.intro: Bringing everyday municipal tasks into a familiar mobile experience.
document.overview: Designed in the YRHacks context, MuniSync explores a connected experience for York Region residents. Its screens cover account setup, study-room and sports bookings, large-item pickup, community notices, and anonymous polls.

children.text: The home screen combines a personal greeting with large cards for bookings, a community poll, filed reports, and upcoming events. The next reservation receives the most prominent space, pairing its time with the room and library. Smaller cards keep participation and service activity within reach.
A persistent bottom navigation gives these different areas a shared structure. Rounded surfaces and distinct colour blocks separate tasks without requiring residents to decode a dense menu.

sections.heading: A dashboard built around the resident
sections.title: Overview

children.text: The study-room flow places the date selector, facility, and filters above the available rooms. Each row pairs a time slot with room capacity and amenity icons, supporting comparison in the same view. Sports bookings follow the same broader pattern of choosing a facility, reviewing details, and confirming.
Confirmation screens collect the selected date, time, and room into a focused summary. A swipe action marks the commitment, followed by a success state that gives the reservation a clear endpoint.

content.alt: MuniSync resident dashboard and study-room availability
content.caption: MuniSync resident dashboard and study-room availability

children.text: The service-request flow explains acceptable pickup items before collecting the request and confirming contact information. Community updates use separate groups for notices, projects, and polls, keeping informational browsing distinct from taking action.

Poll screens explicitly state that submissions are anonymous. Onboarding also explains why the resident's address is needed. These small pieces of contextual copy make the purpose of each interaction visible at the point where residents provide information.

sources.evidence: YRConnect names Winston as creator, links to YRHacks 2024 and its Second Place award, and records the project update on April 18, 2024 at 5:35 PM EDT.
The hacking period starts April 17, 2024, continues in person April 18, and closes April 18.
Submissions open April 17 at 6 PM and close April 18 at 5:30 PM EDT; winners are announced April 18.
YRConnect is listed under April 2024 and identifies YRHacks 2024.
The MuniSync page contains YRConnect onboarding and the matching municipal-app screens.
